note: Voice design briefs for Black Seam. Designed voices, no cloning. Test lines are taken from the prologue script.

voices.description: A man in his late thirties from London, 1869. An engineering draughtsman: educated, lower-middle-class English accent, not posh, not cockney. Low, dry, controlled voice, speaking quietly and close to the listener, as if thinking aloud. Wry and understated, with a cold ambition under the calm. Measured pace with deliberate pauses.
test_lines: Thirty years drawing other men's mines, Josiah, and you were sitting on one.
His field book. By rights it goes in with the rest. ...No. Not yet.
Six feet of steam coal, and nobody alive knows it but me.

voices.description: An elderly English man in his late sixties, chief clerk of a London engineering office in 1869. Thin, dry, slightly reedy voice; precise, clipped, fussy diction. Speaks without looking up, with total confidence in the rules. Disapproving, pedantic, faintly sardonic. Received pronunciation of an older generation.
test_lines: Instruments go out on Mr Hallam's written order, and only on Mr Hallam's written order. Signed for in the book.
From the petty cash, Mr Crane.
Ghosts do not shout up stairwells.

voices.description: A London office boy, about twelve years old, 1869. Strong working-class cockney accent, bright and quick, cheeky but not rude. Young, light voice with lots of energy, a grin in it, always angling for a penny.
test_lines: Mr Bevan used to give me humbugs, sir. Now nobody does.
Mr GRICE! Mr Pike wants you in the strongroom, sir! Urgent!

design.description_used: A London office lad of about eighteen, 1869. Strong working-class cockney accent, bright and quick, cheeky but not rude. Light, youthful voice with lots of energy, a grin in it, always angling for a penny.
